title: Somali Importers Reroute Shipping as Houthi Advances Disrupt Bab-el-Mandeb, Hormuz Traffic
detail: Somalia's business community is shifting away from traditional shipping routes through the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and Strait of Hormuz after Iran-backed Houthi forces captured a strategic Yemeni port city and an island, the Associated Press reported September 13, 2026. Mogadishu Seaport director Mohamed Ali Nur said the port had for the first time received a ship carrying sugar direct from Sri Lanka, calling it a strategy developed in response to the regional tensions. Shipping professional Captain Ali Jemdi said vessels faced trouble transiting the Bab-el-Mandeb because of the war. Somalia depends heavily on maritime trade for food and consumer goods, and longer or rerouted journeys are expected to raise transportation costs and delay deliveries to local markets, compounding the shipping-cost pressure already building since the Iran War began disrupting Gulf of Aden and Red Sea traffic earlier in 2026.

media.caption: Mogadishu port is rerouting shipments as Houthi advances disrupt Bab-el-Mandeb and Hormuz traffic, Sep 13, 2026

title: Ex-Planning Minister Aynte Warns Mogadishu 'Cannot Be Defended' Once AUSSOM Withdraws
detail: Somalia's former Minister of Planning and International Cooperation, Abdirahman Yusuf Hussein Aynte, said publicly on September 13, 2026 that Mogadishu 'cannot be defended' once AUSSOM troop-contributing countries withdraw their forces following the US funding cutoff to UNSOS, the mission's logistics backbone, at the end of 2026. Aynte said US diplomats have told Somali officials that Washington will not reverse the funding decision regardless of the outcome of political negotiations, and that AUSSOM troops cannot remain operationally effective without that logistics chain. He said this assessment is shared privately by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, contrasting it with the president's public remarks on August 16 telling new SNA recruits that Somalia no longer needed foreign peacekeepers and it was time to send them home 'with a bunch of flowers,' and with Mohamud's July 31 Kampala summit appeal to troop-contributing nations to keep their forces in Somalia beyond the funding cutoff.

media.caption: Former Planning Minister Abdirahman Aynte warns Mogadishu cannot be defended without AUSSOM, Sep 13, 2026
